messages:
alyssa: heads-up — nightly perf alert on canary: p50 latency +12%, p99 +18% since merge abc123 (22:10 UTC). dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/nightly/canary
nate: saw it. selector metrics show "generic_conv" path selection jumped from ~8% -> ~46% after abc123. KV hit-rate also dipped ~6pp.
kai: timeline matches. eviction rate spiked ~22:09–22:15. suspect prefetch change in the merge interacting with kernel scoring.
morgan: can you paste the profiler flame for a representative request? quick grep of logs shows a ton of small-kernel fallbacks.
alyssa: pasted minimal profiler snippet below (top stacks collapsed):
```
selector_decision=generic_conv  x  312 ops
  runtime::dispatch_generic
  runtime::attention_generic
  runtime::kv_fetch (miss path)
  kernel::matmul_generic
```
Also prometheus query snapshot:
```
rate(kernel_selector_generic_total[5m]) = 42/min
redis_kv_cache_hit_rate{env=canary} = 0.72 -> 0.66
request_latency_p50{route=/generate} = 120ms -> 134ms
```
jess: @alyssa can we replay the canary traffic locally to repro? if selector has nondet ordering, small differences can blow up.
alyssa: started a replay job: `./infra/replay --since=2026-03-15T22:00Z --dest=local-canary` — will attach traces.
ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout paused for release/2026-03-15-abc123 (auto-pause: latency breach). :warning:
nate: quick root cause hypothesis: the merge changed kernel cost model weights (alpha) and introduced a tie-breaker favoring generic_conv under medium sequence lengths. combined with slightly lower kv hit -> more generic kernels -> longer runtimes.
kai: i ran a small A/B locally toggling alpha back to previous value; selector distribution returned to baseline and p50 dropped ~10ms.
morgan: logs from selector with debug flags:
```
[22:11:02] request_id=.. seq_len=96 cpu_score=0.32 gpu_score=0.41 weighted=0.365 tie_break=0.01 -> chosen=generic_conv
```
if tie_break is too coarse, slight kv variance flips decision.
jess: two immediate remediation options:
- revert abc123 (fast but heavy)
- quick patch: reduce tie_break or bump gpu_score bias for polymorphic kernels (safe short fix)
alyssa: prefer quick patch to avoid revert churn. nate can you open a small PR to adjust tie_break to 0.005 and add an opt-in feature flag for fast revert if needed?
nate: will do. PR branch: perf/selector-tweak-1748809999. patch diff snippet:
```
selector:
  tie_break: 0.005  # reduced from 0.01 to avoid flip on KV jitter
  gpu_bias: 1.05
```
kai: also recommend adding a canary-only metric to surface selector entropy (how often decision changes with minor cache misses).
jess: agreed — add selector_entropy{job=selector} metric, alert if > 0.2 increase.
deploy-bot: ci/perf job queued: run_bench --branch=perf/selector-tweak-1748809999
morgan: replay traces attached: trace_id=tr-00023. initial look confirms more generic_conv calls correlate with missed prefix cache.
alyssa: action items:
- nate: open PR + quick canary patch (ETA 30m)
- kai: add entropy metric and dashboard panel (ETA 2h)
- jess: add perf regression job to CI to run replay against new selector weights (ETA 1h)
- morgan: keep replay running and collect flame graphs (ETA 45m)
we'll reconvene in #eng-runtime in 40m unless patch stabilizes earlier. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: rollout paused, manual resume after canary stable.
